title: How New Drug Pricing Models Will Play Across Europe
gist: US most-favored-nation (MFN) drug pricing links US prices (typically 100%-500% above Europe) to international levels, which BCG estimates could cut profits on future launches to 25%-70% of current levels and pushes pharma toward price convergence, skipping European launches, or bifurcating portfolios. European payers and policymakers must choose between more spending, reallocating to true innovation, or restricting access, and the article argues only coordinated, patient-centered action avoids delayed launches and weaker innovation.

themes.theme: US MFN pricing exports pressure to Europe

insights.claim: US drug prices are in most cases 100% to nearly 500% higher than European prices, so linking US prices to international levels via most-favored-nation (MFN) pricing creates a very large repricing gap for pharma.
insights.speaker: Bernd Ziegler
insights.so_what: The size of the US-EU gap means MFN linkage is a material earnings risk for pharma with US-heavy profit pools.
insights.quote: US drug prices are, in most cases, from 100% to nearly 500% higher than those in Europe.

insights.claim: BCG estimates MFN-driven pressure could cut the profit impact on future pharma launches to 25%-70% of current levels depending on scenario, while drugs already on the market should remain largely unaffected.
insights.speaker: Bernd Ziegler
insights.so_what: Valuation risk sits in pipelines and future launches, not in-market franchises; pipeline-heavy names are more exposed.
insights.quote: we estimate the profit impact on future launches at 25% to 70% of current levels, depending on which scenarios play out

insights.claim: US drug pricing revisions under 2022 legislation signalled a structural reset with sustained downward price pressure rather than a temporary shock, and MFN intensifies that trend by tying US prices to the low end of comparable markets.
insights.speaker: Bernd Ziegler
insights.so_what: Treat US pharma price compression as secular, not cyclical, when modelling long-term margins.
insights.quote: marking a structural reset rather than a temporary policy shock
insights.locator: Incremental changes began earlier this decade

insights.claim: Although framed as a domestic reform, MFN turns the US into a node in global pricing so that actions in one market spill over into others, strengthening international price linkages.
insights.speaker: Bernd Ziegler
insights.so_what: European reimbursement decisions now directly affect US revenue, changing launch economics globally.
insights.locator: Although framed as a domestic reform

insights.claim: The severity of MFN pressure on Europe depends on whether US MFN pricing applies only to government insurance channels or also to private channels, which is being decided through individual confidential company-government agreements.
insights.speaker: Bernd Ziegler
insights.so_what: Watch the scope of company-level MFN deals (public vs private channels) as the key swing variable for exposure.

insights.claim: European responses to MFN are diverging: the UK is adapting to sustain higher drug prices while Germany is doubling down on cost containment, raising risks of unavailable treatments, launch delays and competitive disadvantage.
insights.speaker: Bernd Ziegler
insights.so_what: Expect country-level divergence in launch sequencing; the UK may become a relatively more attractive launch market than Germany.
insights.quote: while some markets (such as the UK) are adapting to sustain higher prices, others (such as Germany) are doubling down on cost containment

themes.theme: Three pharma launch strategies under MFN

insights.claim: Pharma companies can respond to MFN asset by asset with three launch strategies, or combinations: global price convergence, US-EU decoupling, and bifurcation, all of which are problematic.
insights.speaker: Bernd Ziegler
insights.so_what: Use the convergence/decoupling/bifurcation lens to classify each asset's MFN exposure and likely European launch behaviour.

insights.claim: Global price convergence (cutting US launch prices toward European levels while raising prices elsewhere) works best for assets with high unmet need, no established standard of care, sustainable pricing power and smaller MFN price differentials, such as rare-disease treatments.
insights.speaker: Bernd Ziegler
insights.so_what: Rare-disease and high-unmet-need franchises are best placed to defend economics under MFN.

insights.claim: Global price convergence differs from European international reference pricing because the US gap is multiples larger and affects extremely large volumes, so it is likely to significantly shrink the global pool of funds for innovation and pharma profitability.
insights.speaker: Bernd Ziegler
insights.so_what: Convergence implies lower industry R&D budgets and margins, a headwind for biotech funding.
insights.quote: The current difference between prices in the US and Europe is multiples larger, and the volumes affected are extremely large.
insights.locator: There are a couple of significant differences

insights.claim: Under price convergence, European payers facing budget pressure may demand head-to-head trial proof of superiority and introduce tiered access or co-pays, which could let private payers expand supplementary insurance while patients face unequal access.
insights.speaker: Bernd Ziegler
insights.so_what: Private supplementary health insurers in Europe could gain from co-pay and tiered-access models.

insights.claim: US-EU decoupling, where companies skip European launches to avoid low reference prices, is most likely for poorly differentiated assets in areas with established standards of care, such as modern diabetes, cardiovascular and respiratory drugs and oncology 'me too' follow-ons.
insights.speaker: Bernd Ziegler
insights.so_what: Expect fewer or delayed European launches in crowded primary-care categories; European access gaps and reputational risk for pharma follow.

insights.claim: Bifurcation means marketing differentiated, premium-priced treatments in the US while offering lower-priced drugs elsewhere, relevant for highly innovative assets in oncology, immunology, CNS and multi-indication specialty biologics.
insights.speaker: Bernd Ziegler
insights.so_what: Bifurcation raises system complexity but keeps European access to innovation; watch for differentiated portfolio strategies by region.

insights.claim: Bifurcation pushes companies to bring innovations to Europe faster from countries other than the US, notably China, where expertise and innovation rates are rising, requiring multiregional trials, reorganized value chains and IP protections.
insights.speaker: Bernd Ziegler
insights.so_what: China-originated assets licensed into Europe become a growing channel; patients may use different drugs from US vs Chinese makers for the same disease.
insights.quote: In China, for example, expertise and rates of innovation are on the rise.

insights.claim: Each pharma strategy hits European payers differently: price convergence hurts payer budgets hard, US-EU decoupling leaves budgets untouched but could dramatically reduce patient access, and bifurcation forces a change in how drug effectiveness is assessed.
insights.speaker: Bernd Ziegler
insights.so_what: Map payer budget risk by which strategy dominates in each therapeutic area.
insights.locator: Difficult Choices for Payers and Policymakers

insights.claim: European payers have three non-exclusive macro-options under MFN: increase relative spending on innovation, expand total health care spending, or restrict/shape access to innovation, and will likely combine them by therapeutic area.
insights.speaker: Bernd Ziegler
insights.so_what: Each option protects one objective only by costing another; expect mixed, area-specific policies rather than a single reform.

insights.claim: Shifting payer spending toward true innovation raises the value bar via stringent health technology assessment, such as the UK's QALY metric and Germany's AMNOG early-benefit assessment, and cuts budgets for mature and comparable in-market drugs.
insights.speaker: Bernd Ziegler
insights.so_what: Mature or me-too in-market drugs in Europe face reimbursement erosion as payers reallocate to innovation.

insights.claim: Expanding total health spending can be cushioned with value-, population- and outcome-based pricing, tiered access, co-pays, private or individual financing, critical-illness insurance provisions and higher public insurance premiums, a reform under discussion in Germany.
insights.speaker: Bernd Ziegler
insights.so_what: Watch Germany's public insurance premium debate as a signal of willingness to fund innovation.

insights.claim: Payers shaping access will prioritize the neediest patients for high-cost treatments, strengthen outcome- and indication-based reimbursement, and accelerate uptake of generics and biosimilars through clinical guidelines.
insights.speaker: Bernd Ziegler
insights.so_what: Generic and biosimilar makers benefit from payer pushes to steer prescribing under MFN-driven budget stress.

insights.claim: European policymakers can encourage lower-cost alternatives by harmonizing clinical standards and trials for manufacturers in different countries such as the US and China, and by endorsing an EU industry policy that reinforces innovation and price flexibility.
insights.speaker: Bernd Ziegler
insights.so_what: Regulatory harmonization with China would open European markets further to Chinese-originated drugs.

insights.claim: Policymakers must weigh pricing initiatives against the long-term sustainability of national innovation ecosystems, including R&D and manufacturing jobs and value creation.
insights.speaker: Bernd Ziegler
insights.so_what: Aggressive cost containment risks pharma R&D and manufacturing relocation away from Europe.
insights.locator: But it is important not to lose sight

themes.theme: System reset: pricing, funding, innovation interlinked

insights.claim: Pricing, innovation and funding are tightly interconnected parts of one system: increasing health funding relieves pricing pressure and preserves the innovation pool but at significant taxpayer cost, while capped funding forces trade-offs between pricing and innovation.
insights.speaker: Bernd Ziegler
insights.so_what: Model pharma pricing outcomes jointly with fiscal capacity; constrained budgets mean lower innovation returns.
insights.quote: Pricing, innovation, and funding are not independent levers; they are tightly interconnected parts of a single system.

insights.claim: Pharma companies should quickly assess pipelines and market-by-market US and European pricing outlooks, assign each asset a launch strategy, and shift to selective, value-driven innovation with stronger clinical and real-world evidence.
insights.speaker: Bernd Ziegler
insights.so_what: Companies with differentiated pipelines and strong evidence generation should be better positioned under MFN.
insights.locator: Within each part of the ecosystem

insights.claim: Without coordinated collaboration among pharma, payers and policymakers, uncoordinated European responses to MFN risk a race to the bottom of delayed launches, unequal access and weaker innovation; BCG points to the COVID-19 pandemic as precedent for successful ecosystem cooperation.
insights.speaker: Bernd Ziegler
insights.so_what: Signs of EU-level coordination (or lack of it) will determine whether launch delays in Europe materialize.
insights.quote: The changes underway are too big for marginal thinking, and they present an opportunity to build a better system.
insights.locator: Collaboration across the ecosystem is essential
